t: You're looking at St Clement Danes, an Anglican church on the Strand near the Royal Courts of Justice. The first church here was reputedly founded by the Danes in the ninth century. The present building was completed in 1682 by Sir Christopher Wren, then gutted by bombing in the Blitz and restored in 1958 as the central church of the Royal Air Force. That is why airmen are buried here, including Douglas Bader, who flew fighters despite losing both legs, and Sholto Douglas. The Saxon king Harold Harefoot and the writer Mary Pix are buried here too.
